title: India's Biggest Film Is About to Crash San Diego Comic-Con. The Trailer Drop Will Be Historic.
excerpt: Ramayana's ₹4,000-crore epic eyes a Hall H debut this July, with Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, and Sai Pallavi expected in San Diego — and a Hans Zimmer × AR Rahman concert in October.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Ramayana aims for a historic trailer debut at San Diego Comic-Con this July.
  • The film has a budget exceeding ₹4,000 crore, making it one of the most expensive ever.
  • A live concert featuring Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman is planned for October.
  • Ramayana is #1 on IMDb's Most Anticipated Indian Films list for late 2026.
  • Part 1 is set for a Diwali 2026 release, with Part 2 following in 2027.

The biggest Indian film ever made is about to do something no Indian film has done before: unveil itself at San Diego Comic-Con.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=xQCEF5J0KAE

According to a report in Mid-Day, producer Namit Malhotra and director Nitesh Tiwari are in advanced talks with SDCC organizers to debut the official trailer of Ramayana at this month's convention — the same stage where Marvel, DC, and the biggest Hollywood franchises make their global reveals. If the deal closes, it would mark the first time an Indian film has commanded a Hall H-caliber moment at the world's most influential pop culture event.

The move follows a recent focus group screening in Los Angeles, where an early cut of the film reportedly received "highly positive feedback" from a diverse, international audience. That reaction appears to have emboldened the team to go bigger. Much bigger.

> "The feedback has strengthened the belief that the film can travel across cultures," an industry source told Mid-Day.

And the ambition doesn't stop at a trailer. The production is planning a grand musical event in October featuring a live collaboration between Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman — the two Academy Award-winning composers who scored the film together. If that pairing sounds unprecedented, it's because it is. Zimmer, the man behind the scores of *Inception*, *Interstellar*, and *Gladiator*, working alongside Rahman, whose *Slumdog Millionaire* and *Jai Ho* defined a generation of Indian music on the world stage. The October event would showcase their joint work for the first time.

> "The move follows a recent focus group screening in Los Angeles, where an early cut of the film reportedly received "highly positive feedback" from a diverse, international audience."

A ₹4,000-Crore Bet on Ancient India

Ramayana is not a modest undertaking. With a reported budget exceeding ₹4,000 crore (nearly $500 million), it is among the most expensive films ever produced — Indian or otherwise. The two-part epic stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama in what he's called a "once-in-a-lifetime opportunity." During a recent interview with Hollywood press, Kapoor confirmed he's playing a dual role — both Lord Rama and Lord Parashurama — and revealed that shooting for Part 2 is already 50% complete.

Sai Pallavi plays Goddess Sita, KGF star Yash takes on the towering role of Ravana, Sunny Deol is Hanuman, and Ravie Dubey plays Laxman. Arun Govil, who immortalized Lord Rama in the iconic 1987 television series, appears as King Dasharatha — a piece of casting so perfect it feels like destiny.

![Los Angeles — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/Hollywood_Sign_%28Zuschnitt%29.jpg/3840px-Hollywood_Sign_%28Zuschnitt%29.jpg)

Both parts will run over six hours combined, Kapoor confirmed. The visual effects are being handled by DNEG, the Oscar-winning studio behind *Dune*, *Tenet*, and *Inception*.

Why Comic-Con — and Why It Matters for the Diaspora

Comic-Con: A Game Changer
›First Indian film to debut at Hall H.
›130,000+ attendees expected.
›Global media coverage surpasses most film festivals.
›Warner Bros. may handle international distribution.

The choice of Comic-Con is strategic, and the diaspora implications are enormous. SDCC draws 130,000+ attendees and generates global media coverage that dwarfs most film festivals. For an Indian epic rooted in Hindu mythology, securing a slot alongside Marvel and Star Wars isn't just prestige — it's a statement that Indian mythological storytelling belongs on the same stage as Western franchise filmmaking.

For NRIs in the US, UK, and Canada who grew up watching Ramanand Sagar's television Ramayana at their grandparents' homes, the prospect of seeing this story rendered at blockbuster scale — and premiered on American soil — carries a particular emotional charge. Reports suggest that Warner Bros. may be handling international distribution, which would guarantee wide theatrical releases across North America, Europe, and beyond.

The film already sits at #1 on IMDb's Most Anticipated Indian Films list for the second half of 2026, compiled from page views across 250 million monthly visitors. Above Alpha. Above Shah Rukh Khan's King. Above everything.

The Road to Diwali

Ramayana: Part 1 is set for a Diwali 2026 release (likely late October or early November), with Part 2 following exactly one year later at Diwali 2027. If the Comic-Con trailer debut happens as planned, it would set off a five-month campaign unlike anything Indian cinema has attempted — from Hall H in San Diego to a Zimmer-Rahman concert in October to the biggest Diwali release in history.

The teaser, released in April, crossed 18 million YouTube views in 24 hours and set off a firestorm of anticipation. A leaked clip last week — which the production confirmed was real — sparked debate over the VFX quality, but the team has clarified that the footage was from an early, unfinished render.

Release Timeline for Ramayana
July 2026
Trailer debut at San Diego Comic-Con.
October 2026
Hans Zimmer × A.R. Rahman concert.
Diwali 2026
Release of Ramayana: Part 1.
Diwali 2027
Release of Ramayana: Part 2.

The full trailer, whenever and wherever it drops, will be the most scrutinized piece of Indian cinema marketing in years. If it's at Comic-Con, the world won't just be watching India's biggest film. It'll be watching India announce, on the world's biggest stage, that it's done asking for a seat at the table.

It's building its own.
